{{Quote|These gunships fly like butcherbugs and cut into us like Blood Carvers. We must have one.|[[Archduke/Legends|Archduke]] [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]]|<ref name="TNEGtVaV" />}}
The '''Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry (LAAT/i)''', often referred to as the '''Republic attack gunship''' or '''Republic Gunship''', and affectionately known as the "'''larty'''" by [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], was one of the several models in the [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|Low Altitude Assault Transport]] line of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] that mainly served as [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]] and [[Troop transport/Legends|troop transports]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Its role was to transport [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Soldier/Legends|troopers]] as well as offering air-to-ground and air-to-air support for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. The LAAT/i gunship saw extensive use in numerous battles and campaigns of the Clone Wars. During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]], the ships were used by both the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Laati-NEGVV.png|thumb|left|180px|An LAAT/i.]]
The [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|LAAT]]/i was a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] infantry [[Transport/Legends|transport]] capable of carrying up to thirty troopers. Secondary functions included reconnaissance, direct fire support, search-and-recovery, and low-altitude air-to-ground and air-to-air strikes against vehicles ranging from [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeders]] to [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]].

In addition to its trooper complement, housed on a deckplate protected by drooping wings and a sliding side door, the LAAT/i could carry four military [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] in an aft-deployable rack. The crew complement comprised a [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|clone trooper pilot]] and co-pilot/forward gunner in the hunchbacked cockpit, and two auxiliary gunners stationed in pinpoint composite-beam [[Turret/Legends|turrets]] extending on articulated arms from the troop cabin. An [[IM-6 Battlefield Medical Droid/Legends|IM-6 battlefield medical droid]] was commonly carried aboard in an emergency locker. In the event of emergencies, the cockpit capsule could separate from the main craft to act as an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]].<ref name="TCW:TVG" />

The LAAT/i was a fully armed gun platform, with a complete arsenal of weaponry that consisted of three anti-personnel [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser turrets]], two forward-facing, one covering the stern hatch; two top-mounted [[Mass-driver cannon/Legends|mass-driver missile]] launchers fed by rear-mounted ordnance belts and commonly loaded with short-range [[Homing missile/Legends|homing missiles]], HE (high explosive), HEAP (high explosive armor-piercing), and APF (anti-personnel fragmentation) rounds; four composite-beam, pin-point laser turrets, (on some models, the slot for these Balls were inter-changeable with floodlights) two of which were automated bubble-turrets located on either wing; and eight light air-to-air rockets stowed on the underside of each wing.<ref name="CCS" />

Infantry gunships were equipped with atmospheric containment shielding and could be deployed from space, yet could not reach orbit altitude without a carrier vessel. The LAAT/i's optimal fighting range was in the lower atmosphere, where they could reach speeds in excess of six hundred kilometers per hour. A single [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|''Acclamator''-class assault ship]] could carry up to eighty LAAT-series gunships, while a [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] had space for half that complement. The LAAT/i was highly effective but lacked large amounts of armor making it a vulnerable target.

<div style="float:right">[[File:LAATi_snow.png|thumb|180px|LAAT/i [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]] on [[Orto Plutonia/Legends|Orto Plutonia]]]]</div>
When approaching a target, the main cabin would light up red, a visual indicator to stand by, when troopers would conduct last-moment preparations including checking their ammunition and communication systems. Once touching down, the red lights would change to green, signaling clearance to debark.<ref name="TCW">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref>

Within the main cabin were various handles attached to cables hanging from the ceiling of the main cabin. When the gunship's hatches were open, clone troopers would hold on to these to help keep their balance while the gunship was in flight. In the case of rapid deployment, clone troopers could hang on to these as the cables were lowered to the ground for quick deployment so the LAAT/i wouldn't need to land. However, during this process, both the clone troopers and gunship were vulnerable to enemy fire, so landing and debarking in the regular manner was the more common way to deploy troops.

LAAT/i gunships were often a welcome sight for exhausted [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and their [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] commanders.

The assault gunships were capable of being fitted out for stealth missions by the addition of engine baffles and shields, an electromagnetic emission and heat signature-reducing black polymer, as well as the removal of its weaponry. Those modifications made the main hold almost sound proof.<ref name="Speak">{{InsiderCite|139|Speaking Silently}}</ref>

==History==
===New Sith Wars===
[[Odionate]] forces used [[Odionate planetary gunship|gunships visually similar to the LAAT]] during the [[New Sith Wars]], [[1032 BBY/Legends|over a millennium]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. They were sometimes carried into battle by a ship that was visually similar to the [[CR25 troop carrier/Legends|CR25 troop carrier]].<ref name="KEE1">[[Knight Errant: Escape 1|''Knight Errant: Escape'' 1]]</ref> [[Kerra Holt]], disguised as a member of the death cult [[Odion]] cultivated, travelled aboard one of these ships on a mission to [[Sarrassia/Legends|Sarrassia]].<ref name="KEE2">[[Knight Errant: Escape 2|''Knight Errant: Escape'' 2]]</ref>

===Clone Wars===
[[File:MachinesofWar-Textless-EC.png|thumb|left|250px|LAAT/i gunships fly into and deploy clone troopers for the Battle of Geonosis.]]
An early LAAT design was used as a prisoner transport by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] at least [[32 BBY/Legends|ten years]] before the Clone Wars, but the more familiar infantry version gained fame as an air assault vehicle during the war.

The LAAT/i was first deployed in a military operation at the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]],<ref name="SWE2">{{Film|II}}</ref> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]<ref name="NEC" /> where six gunships rescued the surviving [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] from the [[Petranaki arena]] under the command of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]. The gunships proved valuable for the Republic during the battle, eliminating many [[Hardcell-class interstellar transport/Legends|''Hardcell''-class transports]] and clearing the battlefield of many Separatist armored units, especially [[IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank/Legends|''Hailfire'' droids]], which were proving deadly for the Republic [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TEs]].<ref name="SWE2" />

Flights of LAAT/i gunships attempted to disable and destroy many of the fleeing [[Core ship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class core ships]] on the battlefield. During the war, [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] would occasionally pilot the gunships, as demonstrated by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] at Geonosis and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] at the [[Battle of Thule]].<ref name="SW:CW game">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (video game)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' video game]]</ref> Infantry gunships saw continued use throughout the war, with some stationed at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. They would prove pivotal for the Republic many times throughout the brutal conflict, helping win many battles. At some point, the Confederacy unveiled their answer to the LAAT, the [[Mechanized Assault Flyer]],<ref name="BFI">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''</ref> followed by the [[HMP droid gunship/Legends|HMP droid gunship]], both of which matched the LAAT in terms of firepower.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> At some point during the Clone Wars, a least one LAAT/i was deployed with a Clone Trooper unit that include [[Able|BL-1707]] on [[Lubang Minor]], but ended up stranded there, of which the vehicle was later rediscovered by 1 ABY.<ref name="SWE26">[[Empire 26|''Empire'' 26]]</ref>

[[File:ARCgunship_cw21.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The [[Muunilinst 10 LAAT]].]]

====Customization====
During the Clone Wars, many LAAT/i gunships were customized with special paintwork. [[The Muunilinst 10]] had a special gunship assigned to them painted with a blue color scheme and the visage of a rancor across the nose of the ship.<ref name="CW DVD">''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' DVD commentary</ref>

Other gunships, some of which were also individually named, were painted with provocative or morale-boosting artwork on the nose of the ship. Some of the known customized gunships were the [[Lucky Lekku/Legends|''Lucky Lekku'']], [[Crumb Bomber/Legends|''Crumb Bomber'']], [[Spaceward Ho!/Legends|''Spaceward Ho!'']], [[Bantha Poodoo/Legends|''Bantha Poodoo'']], [[Plo's Bros/Legends|''Plo's Bros'']], [[Separatist Nightmare/Legends|''Separatist Nightmare'']], [[Bad Kitty/Legends|''Bad Kitty'']], ''[[Dooku Boot/Legends|Dooku Boot]]'' and [[The Bug Stomper/Legends|''The Bug Stomper'']]. There was also an LAAT/c gunship with a wampa painted on the nose.

===Galactic Civil War===
[[File:Imp_LAAT.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|LAAT]]/i in orbit around [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].]]
Early in the Galactic Civil War, a small anti-Imperial faction, led by former [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], found use for a LAAT/i during their attack on Imperial forces stationed on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]], shortly after the inhabitants of the planet were corrupted by the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark side of the Force]].

Later on, in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] found several disabled, yet still functional, LAAT gunships. The Alliance used these vehicles to further their cause in overthrowing the Empire. When in use by the Rebels, they were known as either "'''Alliance Assault Craft'''" or "'''Rebel Assault Transports'''".<ref name="Battlefront II" /> Other rebel groups not affiliated with the Alliance would also come to rely on the aging military transports, like the [[Jabiimi Loyalists|Jabiimi]]<ref name="SW:Empire" /> and [[Kaminoan resistance|Kaminoan]] rebels.<ref name="Battlefront II" />

During the Galactic Civil War, an Imperial [[Storm commando/Legends|storm commando]] named [[Sarkli]], along with many other [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], [[Battle of Geonosis (Galactic Civil War)|landed]] in a canyon on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] after a skirmish in the asteroid field with [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]]. Sarkli's escape pod landed near a LAAT/i gunship left over from the Clone Wars. The Imperials were attacked by [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]], also from the Clone Wars. Sarkli commandeered the LAAT/i in an attempt to escape the droids. [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], who had also crashed on Geonosis, fought his way through stormtroopers and droids and was attacked and almost killed by Sarkli when he came out of the chaos. The LAAT was severely damaged when Wedge took control of an [[E-Web heavy repeating blaster/Legends|E-Web heavy repeating blaster]]. Swearing revenge on Wedge, Sarkli crashed the LAAT/i into the canyon wall.<ref name="RSIII">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

==Variants==
[[File:LAAT_general_skywalker.jpg|thumb|right|180px|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] discovers a crashed LAAT/i.]]
Rothana Heavy Engineering produced a number of LAAT variants, including the [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/carrier/Legends|LAAT/c]], a carrier gunship capable of delivering [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] and [[TX-130 Saber-class fighter tank/Legends|fighter tanks]] onto the battlefield; the [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/vehicle/Legends|LAAT/v]] with deck space for sixteen speeder bikes or eight military [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]]; and a [[Muunilinst 10 LAAT|command variant]] commonly used by [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Advanced Recon Commandos]]. Some models lacked the bubble turrets on the sides of the deck or had painting on the sides instead such as [[Kowakian monkey-lizard/Legends|Kowakian monkey-lizards]] or [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]]. Non-standard paint schemes appeared more frequently on craft assigned to serve elite units such as [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC Troopers]].

On units that had them, the side-mounted bubble turrets were mounted on armatures that normally held the forward half of the passenger bay doors. As the LAAT/i was equipped with an atmospheric pressure containment shield specifically for use in a vacuum, it was used for various actions in sub-orbital combat situations and also for boarding missions between carrier vessels and enemy cruisers in outer orbit and deep space battles. Bubble turrets were fitted to LAAT/i gunships engaged in combat above the atmospheric ceiling of planets and in space on numerous occasions. At least one longer-range voyage was undertaken by a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/stealth/Legends|LAAT/s]] during the Clone Wars, with bubble turrets fitted in conjunction with fully enclosing, sealed passenger/cargo bay doors. However, the craft crash-landed after atmospheric entry due to complications with weather conditions.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:SWPicsPrototypeGunship.jpg|thumb|left|350px|Early concept art by [[Doug Chiang]], later reused for the [[HMP droid gunship]].]]
The LAAT was inspired by real-world helicopter gunships, notably the [[Wikipedia:Soviet Union|Soviet]] (now [[Wikipedia:Russia|Russian]]) [[Wikipedia:Mil Mi-24|Mil Mi-24 Hind]] [[Wikipedia:Helicopter gunship|helicopter gunship]]. [http://www.starwars.com/databank/vehicle/republicgunship/?id=bts] The ARC LAAT/i's "nose art" was inspired by the decoration found on some real-world combat aircraft such as the [[Wikipedia:Curtiss P-40|Curtiss P-40]] from the 1st AVG Flying Tigers.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref>

[[The LEGO Group]] manufactured four sets of the gunship, one in 2002 for [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] and the second one in 2008 for ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. The third, from 2013 is for [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. The fourth set (2023) is based off of the Coruscant Guard variant, also seen in "The Clone Wars". The first set includes four clone troopers, a [[Droideka/Legends|droideka]], two Super Battle Droids and a generic [[Human/Legends|Human]] Jedi Knight. The vehicle has side bubble turrets, a gun rack and a medical center. The second variation includes Obi-Wan Kenobi, [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]], Commander [[Cody/Legends|Cody]], [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], and a clone trooper. The vehicle has a 74-Z Speeder and a Command Center. The escape pod has been replaced by a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] tank, and the bubble turrets on each side are replaced with two troop bay doors. The second set also includes spy droids and flick-fire missiles. The third set includes a clone trooper pilot, a clone trooper captain, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], two super battle droids, a speeder, and flick-fire missiles. The fourth set includes [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], two regular clone shock troopers, Chancellor Palpatine, and Commander Fox. the fourth set also includes a carrying handle, new stud shooter molds on the tips of each wing, and opening doors on the rear of the vehicle, the front compartment contains nothing, and two storage boxes sit right behind each wing. no side builds are present in the fourth iteration of the Lego gunship.

The [[Knight Errant: Escape 1|11th issue of ''Knight Errant'']] featured ships that looked similar to LAATs. [[John Jackson Miller]] mentioned on his blog that the similarities between the later Republic technology and the ships on display was intentional.<ref name="JJMN1">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknighterrantescape/swknighterrantescape1.html|text=John Jackson Miller's endnotes for Knight Errant Escape issue 1.}}</ref>
